title: Berserk of Gluttony
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a world split between skill-holders and the skill-less, Fate Graphite is a poor gate guard despised for his useless-seeming skill, Gluttony, which leaves him always hungry. When he kills a thief he discovers the skill devours a victim's soul, abilities and stats. Fate must keep feeding it on monsters and enemies to avoid going berserk, while protecting Roxy, a noble holy knight who values effort over birth.
life_message: Even the despised can rise, but power fed by killing must be mastered or it will consume you.

content.note: Killing is the core mechanic: Fate grows by slaying a thief, goblins and stronger foes (Seven Seas blurb via AniList; ANN review). Gore level to verify.
Constant threat of the skill driving Fate berserk; dark fantasy tone (ANN). Capped (to verify).
Romance with Roxy; AniList Female Harem tag (42). Fan service level to verify.
Fate's abuse and daily prejudice (MangaUpdates Abuse category; ANN review); hunger as compulsion.
Revenge against cruel nobles (AniList Revenge tag).
Part of a light novel and anime franchise.

dominant: Rising from caste oppression through power; cost of killing; loyalty to one good noble

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Fate answers years of humiliation personally, and nobles' insults are met with force rather than law.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Fate breaks free of a fixed caste order and acts on his own judgment.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Personal loyalty to Roxy and her house outweighs duty to the realm as a whole.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Skill-based aristocracy is criticized, though Fate serves a noble knight.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Game-like stat systems sit beside holy knights and curses.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Hunger, poverty and staying alive drive every choice.

folkways.japan: Fate's devoted service to Roxy echoes Japanese retainer loyalty, and the stat-and-skill world reflects the Japanese web-novel isekai-style fantasy conventions.

delivery.evidence: ANN review: most elites are terrible people, nobles doubly so, with Roxy the exception (to verify).

personified.ideology: Effort matters more than birth or skill

delivery.note: An ANN review describes the skill hierarchy as a systemic prejudice voiced mostly by cruel elites, with one sympathetic noble.

winners_losers: Fate and Roxy win; cruel skill-holding nobles lose. Sympathy goes to the oppressed underdog, though his power comes at a moral cost the story keeps in view.
